title: Open Questions for AI Engineering: Simon Willison
talk_summary: Simon Willison's 2023 retrospective surveys the first year of LLM engineering: chat interfaces, local models, prompt injection, code interpreter, and CLI pipelines.

takeaways.technique: Treat prompt injection as unsolved; constrain what agents can do rather than filter inputs
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues prompt injection is not solvable by escaping/parameterizing like SQL injection, and that 90% filters fail against adversaries who retry; the practical stance is to limit what an injected agent is permitted to do.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have a lot of 90% Solutions like filtering and trying to spot saxs and so forth but this is a we're up against like malicious attackers here

takeaways.technique: Run model-generated code in a disposable sandbox, not on the host
takeaways.what_they_do: Wants a local code-interpreter equivalent but refuses to execute generated code directly on his machine because of prompt injection; bets on WASM or locked-down containers as the isolation layer.
takeaways.evidence_quote: thanks to things like prompt injection I don't just want to run the code that it gives me in in in just directly on my own computer

takeaways.technique: Composable CLI tools with logged prompts over Unix pipes
takeaways.what_they_do: Builds small CLI tools (llm, jq pipelines) that pipe data between models and log every prompt/response to SQLite, so experiments are reproducible and auditable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: everything that you put through this every prompt and response is logged to a sqlite database so it's a way of building up a sort of research log

takeaways.technique: Ask for attributed quotes so output can be fact-checked
takeaways.what_they_do: When summarizing, requests illustrative quotes with author attribution specifically because quotes can be mechanically cross-checked against the source to detect hallucination.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the thing about asking it for illustrative quotes is that you can fact check them you can cross you can correlate them against the actual content

takeaways.what_they_do: Argues most useful tasks (summarize, extract, RAG) don't need world knowledge, so small models suffice; cites a capable 3B model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I need a model that can work as a calculator for words right I want a model that can summarize text that can extract facts
takeaways.numbers: 3B model described as smallest size doing interesting work

takeaways.technique: Generate work from a backlog of experiments, not ad hoc
takeaways.what_they_do: Maintains a personal research log of every prompt/response and mines it later, treating hoarded experiments as future work supply.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I've now got my own database of summaries of hack and use conversations that I will maybe someday do something with
